name: EasyOCR
notes: Upstream latest on PyPI at probe time: 1.7.2, licence 'Apache License 2.0' (pypi.org JSON API; NOT installed, `version` null). Requires PyTorch, so the install is large. Downloads model weights on first use — that means the first run needs network access, which breaks naive air-gapped or cold-start-sensitive deployments unless you pre-bake the model cache into the image. Model weights carry their own terms separate from the Apache-2.0 code. Easier to get working than PaddleOCR (id 285); generally slower than Tesseract (id 284) on clean printed text but much better on photographed or skewed text. Not installed by instruction: EasyOCR pulls PyTorch and downloads model weights on first use. Readiness stays P1.

name: docTR
notes: PyPI package name is `python-doctr`, not `doctr` — installing `doctr` gets an unrelated project, which is a real and common mistake. End-to-end document text detection plus recognition, aimed at documents rather than scene text. Pretrained weights download separately and carry their own terms. Not installed by instruction: docTR pulls a PyTorch or TensorFlow backend plus downloaded weights. Readiness stays P1.

name: OCRmyPDF
notes: INSTALLED AND MEASURED via Homebrew at 17.10.0. Smoke test passed as a genuine end-to-end pipeline, which is the only way this tool is worth verifying. An image-only PDF was produced with ImageMagick (no text layer — confirmed by pdftotext returning nothing), then `ocrmypdf --output-type pdf` added an OCR layer, and pdftotext on the result returned 'REGISTRY SMOKE'. Installed via the brew `ocrmypdf` formula (52 MB), which pulled Ghostscript 10.07.1 (129 MB) as a dependency — the pip route (`pip install ocrmypdf`) still exists and needs those binaries supplied separately. Licence layering is the thing to get right here, and it is not what the MPL-2.0 field alone suggests: OCRmyPDF's own code is MPL-2.0 (file-level weak copyleft), but it invokes Ghostscript at runtime, and Ghostscript is AGPL-3.0 unless you hold an Artifex commercial licence. The MPL record is OCRmyPDF's own text, recorded verbatim; the AGPL exposure comes in through the dependency, which is why it is flagged rather than folded into the licence field. Review what you actually redistribute. Also requires Tesseract (id 284) — which IS installed here at 5.5.3 — so one of its three dependencies is already satisfied on this machine.
